emitPressureStateTool.ts:264 — `if (!existsSync(snapPath)) return { promoted: false, stale: false };`. Self-correction to UNDECLARED-ALERTCOMMANDER-COLLISION-FIRED-LIVE-FIRST-OBSERVED above. That finding is factually correct (no supersedes on either alert-commander slot) but its implied remedy is wrong. Because supersedes is unimplemented (finding above), adding `supersedes` to alert-commander-critical would produce a config that READS as fixed, satisfies the flow docs, and changes nothing at runtime — both slots would still match and both would still spawn. Any row minted for the alert-commander collision must depend on implementing supersedes first, or choose a different remedy entirely (cron disjunction, or an explicit same-agent guard at Step 4.6).

Stated as an OBSERVED PATTERN, explicitly not a cause. Of the weekday-only ('* * 1-5') slots: healthy are news-scout-sentiment 01:30, chef-morning 05:15, chef-intraday 02-08, alert-commander-market 02-08 — all scheduled BEFORE 08:45Z. Silent are chef-eod 08:45, fb-daily 09:15, market-watcher-eod 16:00 — all AT OR AFTER 08:45Z. Every daily ('* * *') slot is healthy at every hour including 15:00/16:30/17:30/19:45/20:13/21:00. So weekday-only alone is not it, and late-in-day alone is not it; it is the conjunction that partitions. Eliminated so far: catch-up predicate (exonerated 07:45Z — it computes all three correctly and refuses only on rolled_past_vn_date); guaranteed-slot firer alone (see census finding); supersedes (unimplemented, and would cause MORE firing not less). Cause still OPEN — do not assert one. The critical-slot spawn reported it unprompted: 'A concurrent alert-commander session (slot=alert-commander-market) independently ran the same nominal tick=08:00 and raced my notebook Edit... my section was renumbered c225->c226'. VERIFIED by the router, claim holds exactly: file is 31 lines / 8156 bytes, three sections c224(07:45) / c225(08:00 market) / c226(08:00 critical), distinct monotonic NNN, no content loss, tree clean, committed as db899d449 (16+/16-). BUT the two section timestamps are 08:07:00Z and 08:07:04Z — FOUR SECONDS apart. This was won on timing, not on a lock. Do not read the clean outcome as evidence the hazard is handled.

Actionable root cause for the finding above, with two working precedents in-repo. market-watcher HAS `market-watcher-notebook:main` task_claim mutex (eod.md:89, cycle.md:285) added 2026-08-06 by FIX-MARKETWATCHER-EODMD-STALE-NOBASH-CAVEAT-SKIPS-COMMIT-LOSES-NOTEBOOK explicitly to guard the same-agent multi-slot notebook race. news-scout HAS `news-scout-notebook:main` (stage-log-notify.md:24), ported verbatim 2026-08-15. alert-commander has ZERO task_claim of any kind in docs/agents/alert-commander/flow/ — grep returns nothing. The commit-mutex it does use serialises the COMMIT, not the notebook Edit, which is where the race actually is. And alert-commander is the worst-exposed of the three: market-watcher's collision is once per weekday at 16:00Z, whereas alert-commander-critical ('0 */4 * * *') lands inside alert-commander-market ('*/15 2-8 * * 1-5') at BOTH 04:00Z and 08:00Z every weekday — twice daily. Both slots also co-fired at 04:04:10Z today. Remedy: port the established mutex under key `alert-commander-notebook:main`. Unlike declaring `supersedes` (inert — see correction finding), this one is real.

findings.detail: Sharpens this tick's ALERTCOMMANDER-IS-THE-ONE-AGENT-MISSING-THE-NOTEBOOK-MUTEX finding. alert-commander is NOT mutex-less: stage-dispatch-log.md:106 invokes .claude/skills/commit-mutex/SKILL.md. The precise gap is that its mutex is claimed at COMMIT time, after the Edit, so it does not cover the read-highest-c<NNN>-then-append critical section - which is exactly where the collision lives. market-watcher's shipped shape claims market-watcher-notebook:main BEFORE the read and holds it THROUGH the commit (eod.md:89-98, cycle.md:285-307), with bounded 3x retry and proceed-unguarded fallback. news-scout ported the same 2026-08-15. Two shipped precedents for that shape; the remedy is to port it, not to widen the commit-mutex.

The self-authored note's candidate fix is 'route notebook <NNN> assignment through commit-mutex critical section rather than a bare pre-commit file read' - i.e. widen the existing lock. Viable, but it holds a commit-scoped lock across the whole cycle write, and it is NOT the shape that shipped twice in this repo. A future reader of stage-dispatch-log.md:91 will implement the widened-lock variant because that is the only remedy the doc names. If the notebook-mutex port is chosen, that line must be updated in the same change or the doc will contradict the code.

The note claims the race also produced 'a stale c222 retention-cap breach'. Not directly verifiable - the reconciliation landed as one atomic commit, so no mid-race state exists in git. It IS consistent with the pre-state: db899d449^ held exactly c222/c223/c224 (already at the 3-section AC-2 cap), so two concurrent appends force dropping two, which is what db899d449 does (16+/16-, ends c224/c225/c226). Recorded as consistent, not as confirmed.
